title: Five signs a text from your bank is a scam
summary: Scammers copy our name and logo. Here is how to tell a real message from a fake one, and what to do if you clicked.
body:
Text scams are the most common fraud we see. They look urgent and they look like us. Here is what we will never do.

We will never

  • Ask for your online banking password, PIN or a one-time code by text, email or phone
  • Ask you to move money to “protect” it
  • Send you a link to “unlock” your account

If you clicked

Call us right away at (555) 014-2000. We can lock your card in minutes, and the sooner we know, the more we can do.
author: Elena Marsh

title: How to build credit from scratch
summary: No credit history yet? Three ways to start, and how long each one takes.
body:
A credit score needs history. Here are three ways to build it without taking on much risk.

1. A credit-builder loan

We hold the loan amount in savings while you make payments, then release it to you.

2. A secured card

Your deposit is your credit limit. Pay in full each month.

3. Be an authorized user

A family member with good credit can add you to their card.
author: Daniel Okafor

title: Your first home: what to do in the six months before you buy
summary: A month-by-month plan for first-time buyers, from checking your credit to getting preapproved.
body:
Buying a home goes more smoothly when you start early. Here is the plan our mortgage team gives first-time buyers.

Six months out

Check your credit reports for free at annualcreditreport.com and fix any mistakes.

Three months out

Keep saving for the down payment and closing costs. Avoid new car loans or credit cards.

One month out

Get preapproved so you can make an offer with confidence.
author: Priya Natarajan

title: A budget you will actually keep
summary: The 50/30/20 rule, and why it is a starting point, not a rule.
body:
The best budget is the one you look at. Start with three buckets: needs, wants and savings.

  • About half for needs: rent, groceries, insurance, minimum payments
  • About a third for wants
  • The rest for savings and extra debt payments

Then adjust. If rent takes 40% of your pay, that is normal in many places; trim somewhere else.
author: Kestrel Valley staff

title: Certificate ladders, explained
summary: Split your savings across terms so some money is always coming due.
body: A certificate ladder splits your savings across several terms. When the shortest one matures, you renew it at the longest term. After a few years, one certificate matures every year, and you always get long-term rates.
author: Elena Marsh

title: Teaching kids about money, by age
summary: What to teach at 5, 10 and 15, with a few easy activities for each.
body: Money habits start early. At 5, use three jars: spend, save, share. At 10, open a youth savings account together. At 15, practice a monthly budget with a debit card and a low limit.
author: Daniel Okafor

title: Grandparent scams: what to tell older relatives
summary: A caller says a grandchild is in trouble and needs money now. How to slow it down.
body: In a grandparent scam, a caller pretends to be a grandchild, or a lawyer or police officer, and asks for money for bail or a hospital bill. The fix is simple: hang up and call the grandchild or their parent on a number you already have.
author: Priya Natarajan

title: Should you refinance your car loan?
summary: When refinancing saves money, and when it does not.
body: Refinancing makes sense when rates have dropped, your credit has improved, or your first loan came from the dealer at a high rate. Check how many payments are left and whether there is a fee.
author: Kestrel Valley staff
